# Awesome Color Metrics [![Awesome](https://awesome.re/badge.svg)](https://awesome.re)

**Metrics for color and contrast differences between images, sorted by whether they need a pixel-aligned reference, with links to code and toolbox implementations.**

[![metrics](https://img.shields.io/badge/metrics-155-blue)](#metrics) [![with code](https://img.shields.io/badge/with%20code-89-0a7bbb)](CODE.md) [![misalignment-tolerant](https://img.shields.io/badge/misalignment--tolerant-58-2ea44f)](#find-a-metric-by-alignment) [![links checked](https://img.shields.io/badge/links%20checked-2026--10--11-lightgrey)](#about-this-list) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-CC0--1.0-lightgrey)](LICENSE) [![PRs](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen)](CONTRIBUTING.md)

</div>

A curated list of metrics that measure color and contrast differences between two images: color-difference formulas and uniform color spaces, spatial and visibility-based color difference, color-aware quality indices, contrast and tone metrics, learned color-difference measures for photographs, distribution-based and misalignment-robust metrics, white-balance error and test-chart standards. It is organized around one practical question: **does the metric need the reference and the test image to be pixel-aligned?** For every entry the list records how it handles misalignment, whether it actually sees color, what it outputs, and where to get code.

It currently holds **155 entries**, of which **89 have runnable code** (official, toolbox or third-party) and **58 tolerate misalignment** by design, plus 13 datasets. The [interactive page](https://ruilin.li/Awesome-Color-Metrics/) has the same data with search and filters by alignment, color sensitivity and code availability.

**Reading the tables.** Inside each section, entries are grouped by what they need from the image pair. Within a group, entries with code come first, then newest first.

| Alignment group | What it means |
|:--|:--|
| **Needs pixel alignment** | compares values at the same pixel or window; any residual misalignment adds a positive bias |
| **Tolerates small shifts** | designed or shown to tolerate sub-pixel to few-pixel misalignment (coarse scales, anti-aliasing, local search) |
| **Alignment-free** | compares global statistics or distributions, or a per-image measure; position is discarded |
| **Known target** | measured on a test chart against reference values; immune to small shifts when only patch centers are read |
| **Per color pair** | a formula for two colors or one stimulus; whether it needs alignment depends on how you aggregate it |

| Color label | What it means |
|:--|:--|
| **dedicated** | built and validated for color difference |
| **chromatic** | models chromatic channels or color values explicitly |
| **partial** | takes color input but was not designed or tested for color; may miss casts |
| **luminance only** | works on luminance; blind to color casts |

Under the color label is the output type (score, map, components, parameters or text). In the *Code* column, the official repository comes first and toolbox or package implementations follow in small print; "standard" marks a normative document and "—" means no public code was found.

## Color Metrics 101

Write the test image as **I₂(x) = P[ I₁(T(x)) ] + n**: *T* is a geometric misalignment (a nuisance), *P* is the
color / contrast change you want to measure, *n* is noise. A per-pixel metric is only valid when *T* is gone; once a
residual of about one pixel remains, edges start to read as color differences, and because distances are never
negative this error is a **bias** that averaging over images does not remove. The cure is to **average, then
compare**: aggregate over regions or distributions first, compute the difference second. The
[full primer](guide/color-metrics-101.md) explains this with numbers, and [`shift_vs_cast.py`](guide/shift_vs_cast.py)
checks any metric on your own images.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Q{Exact pixel correspondence?} -->|yes, verified| A[Needs pixel alignment<br/>ΔE00 map + ΔL ΔC ΔH, S-CIELAB, FLIP, ColorVideoVDP]
    Q -->|residual around 1 px| B[Average, then compare<br/>block-mean ΔE00, curve + 3x3 fit on block means, MS-SWD]
    Q -->|no, other viewpoint or camera| C[Alignment-free<br/>color distributions, MS-SWD, CD-Flow, CD-Net]
    Q -->|controlled scene| D[Known target<br/>ColorChecker ΔE00, OECF, ISO and CPIQ]
```

| You want to know | Pixel-aligned pair | Misaligned pair |
|:--|:--|:--|
| How much did color change? | per-pixel ΔE00: mean, p95, max, % above threshold | ΔE00 of block means (blocks 16-32× the residual shift) or of image means |
| What changed: lightness, chroma or hue? | per-pixel ΔL\*, ΔC\*, ΔH\* | the same decomposition on block means |
| Which systematic transform? | fit tone curve + 3×3 matrix on pixel pairs | fit on block means; report the fit's ΔE00 on standard colors plus the residual |
| Did contrast change? | local contrast ratio map, tone-curve slopes | Michelson / RMS ratios, distribution distance of band-limited contrast |
| One perceptual number | [Spatial ΔE / VDP](#spatial--visibility-based-color-difference) (ColorVideoVDP, FLIP, iCID) | [Photo color difference](#perceptual-color-difference-of-photographs) (MS-SWD, CD-Flow, CD-Net) |
| Is the metric trustworthy here? | noise floor: two captures with no change | cast-vs-shift test: a visible cast must score far above a 1 px shift |

## Research Threads

- **From uniform patches to photographs.** Classical formulas were fitted to judgments of uniform patches. SPCD (2023) gave 30,000 rated pairs of real phone photos, and learned or distribution-based metrics now outperform per-pixel ΔE on them. <sub>Examples: CIEDE2000 → SPCD / CD-Net → CD-Flow → CD-iNet → MS-SWD → CD-Reasoning</sub>
- **Compare distributions, not pixels.** Tolerance to misalignment comes from discarding position: histograms and optimal transport for colors, patch distributions for local structure, feature statistics, order statistics or Gram matrices for deep features. <sub>Examples: Histogram / EMD → sliced Wasserstein → GPDM → MS-SWD · DISTS → DeepWSD → DOSS → DeepSSIM → DeepDC</sub>
- **Robust is not the same as color-sensitive.** Metrics that normalize local statistics (SSIM, CW-SSIM, deep Gram features) barely react to color casts, so they look stable under shifts for the wrong reason. Report sensitivity to a real change and the reading under misalignment alone. <sub>Examples: SSIM · CW-SSIM · DeepSSIM vs mean ΔE00 · Lab Wasserstein · MS-SWD</sub>
- **Visibility models gain color and displays.** Spatial ΔE grew into display-aware visible-difference predictors with chromatic contrast sensitivity, and into camera-based measurement of real displays with uncertainty estimates. <sub>Examples: S-CIELAB → FLIP → HDR-VDP-3 → castleCSF → ColorVideoVDP → CameraVDP</sub>
- **HDR and wide gamut have no settled ΔE.** PQ-based and appearance-based spaces extend color difference to high luminance and wide gamuts, but new psychophysical data show no model reaches the desired accuracy yet. <sub>Examples: ΔE ITP · Jzazbz · CAM16-UCS · sUCS · PCS26-UCS · Basova 2024</sub>
- **Context, layout and language.** Evidence is growing that averaging point-wise ΔE is not how people judge images: background, spatial pattern and content matter. In parallel, MLLM metrics explain differences in words, though general MLLMs still fail at fine color comparison. <sub>Examples: Becatti 2025 · Baek 2026 · High 2025 · Hammou 2026 · CD-Reasoning · DepictQA · Wu 2024</sub>
- **Other views as the reference.** Novel view synthesis has no ground truth at the test pose, so recent metrics score a rendered view against other views of the scene: cross-attention to nearby views, embeddings that ignore alignment, partial maps completed from the overlap, or a feature distribution of the whole scene. <sub>Examples: Puzzle Similarity → CrossScore → NOVA → PR-IQA → SCODA</sub>

## Metrics

### Color-Difference Formulas & Uniform Color Spaces

Formulas that turn two colors into one number. They know nothing about images: applied per pixel they need exact alignment, applied to region means or distributions they tolerate it. The thread runs from CIELAB ΔE\*ab through CIEDE2000 to color-appearance spaces (CAM16-UCS) and HDR / wide-gamut metrics (ΔE ITP, Jzazbz).

### Spatial & Visibility-Based Color Difference

Per-pixel color difference after modeling human spatial vision: contrast-sensitivity filtering (S-CIELAB, iCID), alternating-image differences (FLIP) and display-aware visible-difference predictors (HDR-VDP, ColorVideoVDP). They output error maps, so they assume pixel correspondence.

**Needs pixel alignment (11)**

| Metric | Venue | Color | Code |

### Color-Aware Full-Reference IQA

General quality indices with a chromatic component, from FSIMc and VSI to LPIPS. They rank distortions well on aligned pairs but fold color, contrast and structure into one score, so they cannot say what changed.

### Perceptual Color Difference of Photographs

Metrics built and validated for color differences between whole photographs, mostly on SPCD (smartphone photos, with a deliberately non-aligned subset). The closest thing to an answer for "how different are the colors" when pixels do not line up.

### Global Statistics & Color Histograms

Classical retrieval-era measures that discard position entirely: color moments, colorfulness, histogram distances and optimal transport between color distributions. Immune to misalignment, blind to where a change happened.

**Tolerates small shifts (1)**

| Metric | Venue | Color | Code |

| **[MPEG-7 color layout](https://doi.org/10.1109/76.927424)**<br>Color and texture descriptors<br><sub>Shrinks the image to an 8×8 grid of mean YCbCr colors, takes the DCT and compares a few low-frequency coefficients (6 for Y, 3 each for Cb and Cr). <i>Note: Coefficient selection as in Kasutani and Yamada, ICIP 2001 (doi:10.1109/ICIP.2001.959135).</i></sub> | IEEE TCSVT 2001 | chromatic<br><sub>score</sub> | — |

**Alignment-free (9)**

| Metric | Venue | Color | Code |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[Sliced Wasserstein distance](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-24785-9_37)**<br>Wasserstein barycenter and its application to texture mixing<br><sub>Projects the 3-D color distributions onto random directions, sorts each 1-D projection and averages the 1-D Wasserstein distances. Same idea as EMD, far cheaper. <i>Note: Theory: Bonneel et al., J Math Imaging Vis 2015 (doi:10.1007/s10851-014-0506-3). Using only the L\*, a\*, b\* axes gives the per-channel 1-D Wasserstein distance.</i></sub> | SSVM 2011 | chromatic<br><sub>score</sub> | <sub>[POT · `ot.sliced_wasserstein_distance`](https://github.com/PythonOT/POT)<br>[this repo · guide/shift_vs_cast.py](guide/shift_vs_cast.py)</sub> |

### Deep-Feature Metrics Robust to Misalignment

Learned or deep-feature metrics designed to tolerate shifts, content misalignment or geometrically disparate references: anti-aliased networks, feature statistics, distribution distances, order statistics, Gram matrices, contextual matching and foundation-model embeddings. Color sensitivity is rarely tested.

**Needs pixel alignment (1)**

| Metric | Venue | Color | Code |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|

### Evaluation Protocols for Misaligned Ground Truth

How papers with imperfect ground truth (learned ISPs, real-world and burst super-resolution, deblurring, stitching, camera-captured displays) actually compute their numbers: align once, align per image with color correction and masks, search shifts, or switch to human ratings.

**Needs pixel alignment (13)**

| Metric | Venue | Color | Code |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[CameraVDP](https://doi.org/10.1145/3757377.3763825)**<br>CameraVDP: perceptual display assessment with uncertainty estimation via camera and visual difference prediction<br><sub>Photographs a display, corrects the camera's geometry, MTF, vignetting and color (one-off spectroradiometer calibration), then runs a visual difference predictor with confidence intervals. <i>Note: Color is calibrated once, not fitted per image to the reference, so display color errors are kept.</i></sub> | SIGGRAPH Asia 2025 | dedicated<br><sub>map</sub> | [GitHub](https://github.com/gfxdisp/CameraVDP)<br><sub>Python</sub> |
| **[BIPNet protocol](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.03680)**<br>Burst image restoration and enhancement<br><sub>Follows the BurstSR real-data protocol (flow alignment, color correction, masking) for burst super-resolution, plus standard metrics for denoising and low-light enhancement.</sub> | CVPR 2022 | partial<br><sub>score</sub> | [GitHub](https://github.com/akshaydudhane16/BIPNet)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[SelfDZSR protocol](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.01325)**<br>Self-supervised learning for real-world super-resolution from dual zoomed observations<br><sub>Matches the color and brightness of the ground truth to the input, warps it to the input, then computes full-reference metrics.</sub> | ECCV 2022 | partial<br><sub>score</sub> | [GitHub](https://github.com/cszhilu1998/SelfDZSR)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[Deep Burst SR protocol](https://doi.org/10.1109/CVPR46437.2021.00909)**<br>Deep burst super-resolution<br><sub>Aligns the output to the ground truth with PWC-Net optical flow, fits a 3×3 color matrix on Gaussian-smoothed images, masks invalid pixels, then computes PSNR / SSIM / LPIPS. <i>Note: Smoothing before fitting the color matrix is "average, then compare"; but the fitted color difference is removed, not reported.</i></sub> | CVPR 2021 | partial<br><sub>score</sub> | [GitHub](https://github.com/goutamgmb/deep-burst-sr)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[LiteISPNet protocol](https://doi.org/10.1109/ICCV48922.2021.00431)**<br>Learning RAW-to-sRGB Mappings with Inaccurately Aligned Supervision<br><sub>Aligns outputs to the target geometrically only, without color correction, and also reports the unaligned numbers.</sub> | ICCV 2021 | partial<br><sub>score</sub> | [GitHub](https://github.com/cszhilu1998/RAW-to-sRGB)<br><sub>PyTorch</sub> |
| **[DRealSR protocol](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.01928)**<br>Component divide-and-conquer for real-world image super-resolution<br><sub>Five-DSLR multi-focal-length SR benchmark; SIFT then iterative patch registration with brightness matching and manual checks; PSNR on Y, SSIM / LPIPS on RGB.</sub> | ECCV 2020 | partial<br><sub>score</sub> | [GitHub](https://github.com/xiezw5/Component-Divide-and-Conquer-for-Real-World-Image-Super-Resolution) |
| **[PyNET protocol](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.05509)**<br>Replacing Mobile Camera ISP with a Single Deep Learning Model<br><sub>SIFT + RANSAC global alignment of phone RAW and DSLR photos, then a small shift / rotation search per 448×448 patch; patches with cross-correlation below 0.9 are discarded. <i>Note: The residual misalignment is assumed equal for all methods; absolute color errors are inflated by it.</i></sub> | CVPRW 2020 | partial<br><sub>score</sub> | [GitHub](https://github.com/aiff22/PyNET) |
| **[RealBlur protocol](http://cg.postech.ac.kr/research/RealBlur/)**<br>Real-world blur dataset for learning and benchmarking deblurring algorithms<br><sub>Evaluation script aligns each result to the ground truth with an ECC homography, scales intensity and masks invalid borders before PSNR / SSIM. <i>Note: Intensity scaling only; no color correction.</i></sub> | ECCV 2020 | partial<br><sub>score</sub> | [GitHub](https://github.com/rimchang/RealBlur) |
| **[RealSR protocol](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.00523)**<br>Toward real-world single image super-resolution: a new benchmark and a new model<br><sub>Captures LR / HR pairs by changing focal length, registers them iteratively with mean / std luminance adjustment, then computes PSNR / SSIM on the Y channel.</sub> | ICCV 2019 | luminance only<br><sub>score</sub> | [GitHub](https://github.com/csjcai/RealSR) |
| **[ECC alignment](https://doi.org/10.1109/TPAMI.2008.113)**<br>Parametric image alignment using enhanced correlation coefficient maximization<br><sub>Estimates a parametric warp by maximizing a correlation coefficient that is invariant to global brightness and contrast, the registration step behind several benchmarks. <i>Note: Photometric differences are cancelled, not estimated, so the warp step hides part of what a color metric should measure.</i></sub> | IEEE TPAMI 2008 | luminance only<br><sub>parameters</sub> | <sub>[OpenCV · `findTransformECC`](https://github.com/opencv/opencv)</sub> |
| **[MAI 2021 ISP protocol](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.07809)**<br>Learned smartphone ISP on mobile NPUs with deep learning, Mobile AI 2021 challenge: report<br><sub>Phone RAW and Fujifilm sRGB are aligned with a dense correspondence network before PSNR / SSIM fidelity scoring and runtime measurement on NPUs.</sub> | CVPRW 2021 | partial<br><sub>score</sub> | — |
| **[NTIRE 2021 Burst SR protocol](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.03839)**<br>NTIRE 2021 challenge on burst super-resolution: methods and results<br><sub>The real-data track uses the aligned, color-corrected PSNR / SSIM / LPIPS of Deep Burst SR.</sub> | CVPRW 2021 | partial<br><sub>score</sub> | — |

### White Balance & Illuminant Error

Errors between an estimated and a true illuminant or white point. A single chromaticity vector per image, so alignment does not matter; the debate is about which error matches what viewers see.

**Alignment-free (5)**

| Metric | Venue | Color | Code |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **[Recovery angular error](https://doi.org/10.1364/JOSAA.23.001008)**<br>Reevaluation of color constancy algorithm performance<br><sub>Angle between estimated and true illuminant RGB vectors, independent of intensity; argues for summarizing errors by the median rather than the mean and for statistical tests when comparing algorithms. <i>Note: Per-pixel RGB angles between two images are unstable in dark regions; compare region or image means instead.</i></sub> | JOSA A 2006 | dedicated<br><sub>score</sub> | <sub>[this repo · guide/shift_vs_cast.py](guide/shift_vs_cast.py)</sub> |
| **[Beyond angular error](https://doi.org/10.1002/col.70084)**<br>Beyond angular error: rethinking metric for white balance and its effect on image color appearance<br><sub>Splits the illuminant error in the camera (R/G, B/G) plane into components along and perpendicular to the Planckian locus and weights the perpendicular one more, matching color-appearance error better than angular error. <i>Note: Evidence comes from ColorChecker CIELAB ΔE, not a psychophysical experiment.</i></sub> | Color Res Appl 2026 | dedicated<br><sub>components</sub> | — |
| **[MIS acceptability](https://doi.org/10.2352/cic.2025.33.1.6)**<br>Testing the acceptability prediction of color difference models using the Multiple Illumination Scenarios (MIS) dataset<br><sub>3,465 acceptability ratings of white-balance shifts in single- and multi-illuminant scenes; dark and low-chroma regions are more sensitive, motivating two corrections to color-difference formulas.</sub> | CIC 2025 | dedicated<br><sub>score</sub> | — |
| **[Reproduction angular error](https://doi.org/10.1109/TPAMI.2016.2582171)**<br>The reproduction angular error for evaluating the performance of illuminant estimation algorithms<br><sub>Angle between the white surface as reproduced with the estimated illuminant and true achromatic white, which tracks the visible error in the corrected image rather than in the illuminant. <i>Note: First proposed at BMVC 2014 (doi:10.5244/C.28.70).</i></sub> | IEEE TPAMI 2017 | dedicated<br><sub>score</sub> | — |
| **[Perceptual illuminant distances](https://doi.org/10.1364/JOSAA.26.002243)**<br>Perceptual analysis of distance measures for color constancy algorithms<br><sub>Psychophysical test of how well distance measures between estimated and true illuminants, angular error among them, predict observers' judgments of the corrected images.</sub> | JOSA A 2009 | dedicated<br><sub>score</sub> | — |

### Test Charts & Camera Standards

Metrics computed on targets with known reference values: ColorChecker ΔE, OECF / tone curve, noise and dynamic range, shading, slanted-edge SFR and dead-leaves texture. Reading only the center of each patch makes them immune to small misregistration.

**Needs pixel alignment (2)**

| **[Dead leaves misregistration](https://doi.org/10.2352/issn.2470-1173.2017.12.iqsp-257)**<br>The effects of misregistration on the dead leaves cross-correlation texture blur analysis<br><sub>Shows that misregistration as small as 0.15 px makes the real part of the cross-correlation MTF fluctuate strongly, and recommends the magnitude of the transfer function instead.</sub> | IS&T EI 2017 | luminance only<br><sub>components</sub> | — |
| **[Intrinsic dead leaves](https://doi.org/10.1117/12.2039689)**<br>Description of texture loss using the dead leaves target: current issues and a new intrinsic approach<br><sub>Cross-spectrum between the captured image and the known chart pattern; robust to noise and recovers phase, but the reference must be registered exactly.</sub> | Proc SPIE 2014 | luminance only<br><sub>components</sub> | — |

| **[ColorChecker ΔE](https://www.babelcolor.com/colorchecker-2.htm)**<br>A color-rendition chart<br><sub>Mean and maximum ΔE00 over the 24 patches, plus ΔC00 (no lightness), saturation ratio and gray-patch white-balance error; patch centers only. <i>Note: Paper: McCamy, Marcus and Davidson, J Appl Photogr Eng 2(3):95–99. The link gives reference data; the pigments changed in Nov 2014 (mean ΔE00 0.85 between versions), so match your chart.</i></sub> | J Appl Photogr Eng 1976 | dedicated<br><sub>components</sub> | <sub>[colour-checker-detection](https://github.com/colour-science/colour-checker-detection)<br>[OpenCV contrib · `mcc`](https://github.com/opencv/opencv_contrib/tree/4.x/modules/mcc)</sub> |
| **[ISO 12233 SFR](https://www.iso.org/standard/88626.html)**<br>ISO 12233:2024 Digital cameras — Resolution and spatial frequency responses<br><sub>Slanted-edge SFR (contrast transfer vs spatial frequency) with 4× oversampled edge profiles; the edge position is fitted from the data, so ROI shifts do not matter. <i>Note: Algorithm background: Burns, PICS 2000; edition-4 update (polynomial edge fit, Tukey window): Burns et al., IS&T EI 2022 (doi:10.2352/ei.2022.34.9.iqsp-357).</i></sub> | ISO 2024 | luminance only<br><sub>components</sub> | standard<br><sub>[sfrmat (MATLAB, BSD)](http://burnsdigitalimaging.com/software/sfrmat/)<br>[MTF Mapper (C++, BSD)](https://sourceforge.net/projects/mtfmapper/)</sub> |
| **[IEEE 1858 CPIQ](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1858/6931/)**<br>IEEE 1858-2023 Standard for Camera Phone Image Quality (CPIQ)<br><sub>Phone camera metrics (spatial frequency response, color uniformity, chroma level, lateral chromatic displacement, distortion, texture blur, visual noise), each converted to JND of quality loss. <i>Note: DOI 10.1109/IEEESTD.2023.10205967; supersedes IEEE 1858-2016.</i></sub> | IEEE Std 2023 | chromatic<br><sub>components</sub> | standard |
| **[ISO 15739 noise](https://www.iso.org/standard/82233.html)**<br>ISO 15739:2023 Photography — Electronic still-picture imaging — Noise measurements<br><sub>Signal-to-noise ratio, visual noise (opponent space with per-channel CSF weighting) and noise-limited dynamic range from uniform patches.</sub> | ISO 2023 | chromatic<br><sub>components</sub> | standard |
| **[ISO/TS 19567-2 dead leaves](https://www.iso.org/standard/70955.html)**<br>ISO/TS 19567-2:2019 Photography — Digital cameras — Texture reproduction measurements — Part 2: Texture analysis using stochastic pattern<br><sub>Texture MTF from a dead-leaves (random occluding disks) chart, which exposes adaptive noise reduction that a slanted edge misses.</sub> | ISO/TS 2019 | luminance only<br><sub>components</sub> | standard |
| **[ISO 17957 shading](https://www.iso.org/standard/31974.html)**<br>ISO 17957:2015 Photography — Digital cameras — Shading measurements<br><sub>Luminance and color shading (non-uniformity across the field) measured on a uniform target.</sub> | ISO 2015 | chromatic<br><sub>map</sub> | standard |
| **[ISO 19084 chromatic displacement](https://www.iso.org/standard/63894.html)**<br>ISO 19084:2015 Photography — Digital cameras — Chromatic displacement measurements<br><sub>Defines chromatic displacement (the offset between color channels at the same edge, i.e. lateral chromatic aberration) and the test patterns, conditions and procedures for measuring it from camera output images. <i>Note: Sets no pass / fail limit; testing software is distributed through imaging.org. Confirmed in 2025.</i></sub> | ISO 2015 | chromatic<br><sub>parameters</sub> | standard |
| **[ISO 17321-1](https://www.iso.org/standard/56537.html)**<br>ISO 17321-1:2012 Graphic technology and photography — Colour characterisation of digital still cameras (DSCs) — Part 1: Stimuli, metrology and test procedures<br><sub>Stimuli, measurements and procedures for characterizing a camera's color response, i.e. fitting the camera-RGB-to-XYZ transform from targets.</sub> | ISO 2012 | dedicated<br><sub>parameters</sub> | standard<br><sub>[colour · `colour.characterisation`](https://github.com/colour-science/colour)</sub> |
| **[ISO 14524 OECF](https://www.iso.org/standard/43527.html)**<br>ISO 14524:2009 Photography — Electronic still-picture cameras — Methods for measuring opto-electronic conversion functions (OECFs)<br><sub>Measures the tone curve (opto-electronic conversion function) from a gray-scale chart, i.e. the camera's contrast transfer from scene luminance to output values.</sub> | ISO 2009 | luminance only<br><sub>parameters</sub> | standard |
| **[Mahalanobis color separation](https://doi.org/10.2352/ei.2026.38.16.avm-112)**<br>Mahalanobis distance as a robust color (signal) separation metric<br><sub>Noise-referenced separability of two color patches using the pooled noise covariance; invariant to white balance, CCM and other linear steps, unlike ΔE2000 or Δa\*b\*.</sub> | IS&T EI 2026 | chromatic<br><sub>score</sub> | — |
| **[CPIQ spatial metrics](https://doi.org/10.1117/12.905752)**<br>Development of the I3A CPIQ spatial metrics<br><sub>How the CPIQ edge acutance, texture acutance and visual noise metrics were built from opponent-space CSF weighting and display / print MTFs.</sub> | Proc SPIE 2012 | chromatic<br><sub>score</sub> | — |
| **[Visual noise metric](https://doi.org/10.1117/12.871633)**<br>Development of a perceptually calibrated objective metric of noise<br><sub>Objective noise metric calibrated in just-noticeable differences with a softcopy quality-ruler experiment on simulated phone noise.</sub> | Proc SPIE 2011 | chromatic<br><sub>score</sub> | — |
| **[Dead leaves texture MTF](https://doi.org/10.1117/12.838902)**<br>Dead leaves model for measuring texture quality on a digital camera<br><sub>Texture MTF as the square root of the ratio of output to chart power spectra on a scale-invariant dead-leaves pattern; power spectra ignore phase, so position does not matter. <i>Note: Earlier version: Cao, Guichard and Hornung, Proc SPIE 7250, 2009 (doi:10.1117/12.805853).</i></sub> | Proc SPIE 2010 | luminance only<br><sub>components</sub> | — |
| **[Noise-corrected dead leaves](https://doi.org/10.1117/12.838698)**<br>Texture-based measurement of spatial frequency response using the dead leaves target: extensions, and application to real camera systems<br><sub>Subtracts the noise power measured on uniform patches from the output spectrum before forming the texture MTF. <i>Note: Assumes noise on gray patches equals noise on texture, which adaptive noise reduction breaks.</i></sub> | Proc SPIE 2010 | luminance only<br><sub>components</sub> | — |

### Benchmarks, Psychophysics & Surveys

Evaluations of the metrics themselves: psychophysical tests of color-difference models, comparisons of histogram distances and retargeting metrics, MLLM benchmarks, and surveys of color image quality assessment.

| Paper | Venue | Code |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **[STRESS](https://doi.org/10.1364/JOSAA.24.001823)**<br>Measurement of the relationship between perceived and computed color differences<br><sub>The STRESS index (0 is perfect) for testing a color-difference formula against visual data, with a statistical test for whether two formulas differ significantly.</sub> | JOSA A 2007 | <sub>[colour · `index_stress`](https://github.com/colour-science/colour)</sub> |
| **[ISO 20462-3 quality ruler](https://www.iso.org/standard/54617.html)**<br>ISO 20462-3:2012 Photography — Psychophysical experimental methods for estimating image quality — Part 3: Quality ruler method<br><sub>Observers place a test image against a calibrated series of ruler images, giving scores on the Standard Quality Scale (SQS), whose unit is one just-noticeable difference; parts 1 and 2 cover the overview and the triplet comparison method. <i>Note: The JND scale of IEEE 1858 CPIQ is calibrated with this kind of experiment.</i></sub> | ISO 2012 | standard |
| **[Hue non-uniformity perception](https://doi.org/10.17289/jkscs.40.3.2026.08.81)**<br>A study on hue non-uniformity perception in the display – comparing perceptual data and color difference models<br><sub>2AFC experiment on display color non-uniformity; perception depends on the spatial pattern of the differences, not only their mean, and neither CIEDE2000 nor a CSF-filtered variant predicts it fully.</sub> | J Korea Soc Color Stud 2026 | — |
| **[Low-level vision tests of metrics](https://doi.org/10.1109/qomex69967.2026.11618380)**<br>Evaluating quality metrics through the lenses of psychophysical measurements of low-level vision<br><sub>Tests 34 metrics against contrast-sensitivity, masking and matching data; CIEDE2000 and HyAB are far more sensitive to achromatic than to chromatic contrast, while S-CIELAB, FLIP, MS-SWD and ΔE ITP behave the opposite way. <i>Note: arXiv:2503.16264.</i></sub> | QoMEX 2026 | — |
| **[Uniformity error for color spaces](https://doi.org/10.2352/ei.2026.38.10.hvei-237)**<br>A perceptual uniformity error metric for standard and high dynamic range colour spaces<br><sub>An error metric for how perceptually uniform a standard or HDR color space is.</sub> | IS&T EI 2026 | — |
| **[VLM psychophysics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.24578)**<br>Evaluating vision-language models for image quality assessment using psychophysical data<br><sub>Controlled paired comparisons of contrast, colorfulness and preference show that VLM agreement with observers varies by attribute and that high self-consistency does not imply perceptual accuracy.</sub> | CIC 2026 | — |
| **[Color difference in context](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-72845-7_4)**<br>Color difference in context: an experiment<br><sub>The same color pair on different backgrounds gives very different judged differences, suggesting that refining point-wise formulas further is of limited use without context.</sub> | CCIW (LNCS) 2025 | — |
| **[Color IQA survey](https://doi.org/10.3390/jimaging11090307)**<br>Research progress on color image quality assessment<br><sub>Survey of color image quality assessment methods, data sets and open problems.</sub> | J Imaging 2025 | — |
| **[MLLM IQA study](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-72904-1_9)**<br>A comprehensive study of multimodal large language models for image quality assessment<br><sub>Benchmarks MLLMs on quality tasks; on SPCD color differences GPT-4V reaches an SRCC of only 0.122 and all models struggle with fine-grained comparison.</sub> | ECCV 2024 | — |
| **[WCG / HDR ΔE evaluation](https://doi.org/10.3390/jimaging10120317)**<br>Evaluation of color difference models for wide color gamut and high dynamic range<br><sub>New psychophysical data over wide gamut, high luminance and small-to-large differences; CAM16-UCS with a power correction generalizes best up to 1611 cd/m², but no model reaches the desired accuracy.</sub> | J Imaging 2024 | — |
| **[ΔE survey](https://mgv.sggw.edu.pl/mgv20)**<br>Color difference ΔE - A survey<br><sub>Review of perceptually uniform color spaces and ΔE formulas up to CIEDE2000, discussing when two colors should be judged similar or distinct.</sub> | Mach Graph Vis 2011 | — |
| **[RetargetMe](https://doi.org/10.1145/1882261.1866186)**<br>A comparative study of image retargeting<br><sub>User study of retargeting methods and of metrics that compare images with very different geometry; EMD and SIFT-flow rankings agree best with users, ahead of BDS and edge histograms.</sub> | ACM TOG (SIGGRAPH Asia) 2010 | — |
| **[Histogram distance benchmark](https://doi.org/10.1109/iccv.1999.790412)**<br>Empirical evaluation of dissimilarity measures for color and texture<br><sub>Large-scale comparison of nine distribution dissimilarity measures (χ², Kolmogorov-Smirnov, EMD, quadratic form, intersection, ...) for color and texture classification, retrieval and segmentation.</sub> | ICCV 1999 | — |

## Datasets

| Dataset | Year | Content | Size | Used for | Link |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| **CIEDE2000 test data**<br><sub>Sharma, Wu, Dalal</sub> | 2005 | Color pairs with reference ΔE00 values chosen to expose implementation errors | 34 pairs | Validating any CIEDE2000 implementation | [link](https://hajim.rochester.edu/ece/sites/gsharma/ciede2000/) |
| **CID:IQ**<br><sub>Liu, Pedersen, Hardeberg</sub> | 2014 | 23 references × 6 distortions (including two gamut-mapping methods) × 5 levels, rated by 17 observers | 690 distorted images | Image-difference and gamut-mapping quality metrics | [link](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.17376246) |
| **KADID-10k**<br><sub>Lin, Hosu, Saupe</sub> | 2019 | 81 references × 25 distortion types × 5 levels; color category with color diffusion, color shift, color quantization and two saturation changes | 10,125 distorted images | Testing FR-IQA on synthetic color distortions | [link](https://database.mmsp-kn.de/kadid-10k-database.html) |
| **TID2013**<br><sub>Ponomarenko et al.</sub> | 2015 | 25 references × 24 distortion types × 5 levels; color-related types are noise in color components, saturation change, color quantization and chromatic aberration | 3,000 distorted images | Testing FR-IQA, including color distortions | [link](https://www.ponomarenko.info/tid2013.htm) |
| **TMQ-ME**<br><sub>TM metric adaptation</sub> | 2026 | HDR references with tone-mapped SDR versions focused on basic tone-mapping operations, with quality scores | 3.04 GB (EXR) | Evaluating metrics for tone-mapped content | [link](https://doi.org/10.17863/CAM.129808) |
| **castleCSF data**<br><sub>castleCSF</sub> | 2024 | Contrast-detection thresholds pooled from 18 studies, any color direction, luminance and size | CSV tables | Fitting and testing chromatic / achromatic contrast-sensitivity models | [link](https://github.com/gfxdisp/castleCSF) |
| **SPCD**<br><sub>CD-Net</sub> | 2023 | Same scenes shot with six flagship phones (10k pairs only globally registered) plus ~20k aligned pairs from editing tools, filters and wrong color profiles | 15,335 images, 30,000 rated pairs | Main benchmark for photographic color difference, including a non-aligned subset (CD-Net, CD-Flow, MS-SWD, CD-Reasoning); Baidu Netdisk, code txeh (the Google Drive copy is gone) | [link](https://pan.baidu.com/s/18bzu-qhpMW3PqLTlVdoZRQ?pwd=txeh) |
| **CFD (Color Fidelity Dataset)**<br><sub>CFM</sub> | 2026 | Real photographs and text-to-image generations arranged in ordered levels of color realism | over 1.3M images | Training and testing color-fidelity (realism) scores for generated images | [link](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Nineve/CFD_dataset) |
| **NVS-NAR-IQA**<br><sub>NOVA</sub> | 2026 | Novel views rendered by three NeRF and two Gaussian-splatting models on 17 NeRFStudio scenes, judged against an aligned or a nearby non-aligned reference view | 1,035 triplets with expert forced-choice votes | Testing metrics that accept non-aligned references (NOVA, CrossScore, ST-LPIPS); access via a Google Form | [link](https://live.ece.utexas.edu/research/NVS_NAR_IQA/NVS-NAR-IQA.html) |
| **NIGHTS**<br><sub>DreamSim</sub> | 2023 | Synthetic image triplets with human similarity votes | 20k triplets (58 GB) | Training and testing embedding-based similarity | [link](https://github.com/ssundaram21/dreamsim) |
| **PIPAL**<br><sub>Gu et al.</sub> | 2020 | Outputs of traditional and GAN-based restoration with human ratings; GAN outputs often contain small misalignments | 250 references, ~29k distorted images | Metrics that tolerate texture and small geometric differences (MIPM, DISTS-style metrics) | [link](https://github.com/HaomingCai/PIPAL-dataset) |
| **ColorChecker reference data**<br><sub>BabelColor</sub> | 2014 | L\*a\*b\* and average spectra of the 24 patches, for charts made before and after November 2014 | Text / CGATS files | Reference values for ColorChecker ΔE | [link](https://www.babelcolor.com/colorchecker-2.htm) |
| **RetargetMe**<br><sub>Rubinstein et al.</sub> | 2010 | Images retargeted by several methods with user-study rankings | — | Metrics for references with very different geometry (DeepSSIM, BDS, EMD) | [link](https://people.csail.mit.edu/mrub/retargetme/) |

## Tools & Libraries

**Color Science Libraries**

- [colour](https://github.com/colour-science/colour) - Color science toolbox with every common ΔE (CIE 1976 / 1994 / 2000, CMC, DIN99, ITP, CAM02 / CAM16-UCS, HyAB, HyCH), uniform spaces (Jzazbz, ZCAM, sUCS, Oklab), camera characterization and the STRESS index. <sub>Python</sub>
- [scikit-image](https://github.com/scikit-image/scikit-image) - Lab conversion plus `deltaE_cie76`, `deltaE_ciede94`, `deltaE_ciede2000`, `deltaE_cmc` and `structural_similarity`. <sub>Python</sub>
- [ciede2000-color-matching](https://github.com/michel-leonard/ciede2000-color-matching) - Public-domain CIEDE2000 implementations with shared test suites. <sub>40+ languages</sub>
- [coloraide](https://github.com/facelessuser/coloraide) - Color manipulation library with many color spaces and ΔE methods. <sub>Python</sub>
- [culori](https://github.com/Evercoder/culori) - Color library for the web with color-difference functions. <sub>JavaScript</sub>
- [OpenCV](https://github.com/opencv/opencv) - `compareHist` (intersection, χ², Bhattacharyya), `EMD`, and `findTransformECC` for photometric-invariant registration. <sub>C++ / Python</sub>

**IQA & Distance Toolboxes**

- [pyiqa (IQA-PyTorch)](https://github.com/chaofengc/IQA-PyTorch) - Largest IQA toolbox; includes `msswd`, `fsim`, `vsi`, `cw_ssim`, `lpips`, `stlpips`, `dists`, `deepdc`, `pieapp`, `ms_ssim` and `gmsd`. Non-commercial license. <sub>PyTorch</sub>
- [piq](https://github.com/photosynthesis-team/piq) - IQA metrics and losses, including FSIM, VSI, MDSI, GMSD, HaarPSI, LPIPS, DISTS and PieAPP. <sub>PyTorch</sub>
- [POT](https://github.com/PythonOT/POT) - Python Optimal Transport; exact EMD, 1-D Wasserstein and sliced Wasserstein distances for color or patch distributions. <sub>Python</sub>

**Standalone Perceptual Difference Tools**

- [ColorVideoVDP](https://github.com/gfxdisp/ColorVideoVDP) - Display-aware visible-difference predictor for images and video (`pip install cvvdp`); also hosts ColorVideoVDP-ML and PU-PSNR. <sub>PyTorch</sub>
- [HDR-VDP](https://sourceforge.net/projects/hdrvdp/) - HDR-VDP-3 (quality, visibility and contrast-distortion predictions from photometric input). <sub>MATLAB / Octave</sub>
- [FLIP](https://github.com/NVlabs/flip) - LDR and HDR FLIP error maps (`pip install flip-evaluator`). <sub>Python / C++ / CUDA</sub>
- [Butteraugli](https://github.com/google/butteraugli) - Psychovisual difference score and spatial difference map aimed at barely noticeable differences, used in JPEG XL encoding. <sub>C++</sub>
- [SSIMULACRA 2](https://github.com/cloudinary/ssimulacra2) - Perceptual metric for compression artifacts computed in a perceptual color space, tuned on CID22, TID2013, KADID-10k and KonFiG-IQA. <sub>C++</sub>

**Test-Chart Analysis**

- [colour-checker-detection](https://github.com/colour-science/colour-checker-detection) - Detects ColorChecker charts and extracts patch colors. <sub>Python</sub>
- [sfrmat](http://burnsdigitalimaging.com/software/sfrmat/) - Reference slanted-edge SFR implementation for ISO 12233 by Peter Burns (BSD). <sub>MATLAB</sub>
- [MTF Mapper](https://sourceforge.net/projects/mtfmapper/) - Open-source slanted-edge MTF measurement (BSD). <sub>C++</sub>
- [Imatest Colorcheck docs](https://docs.imatest.com/docs/colorcheck) - Documentation of chart-based ΔE00, ΔC00 and saturation measurements; useful even without the software. <sub>commercial</sub>
- [iQ-Analyzer-X](https://www.image-engineering.de/en/products/software/iq-analyzer-x) - Commercial analysis of SFR, texture, OECF, color, shading, distortion and noise charts. <sub>commercial</sub>

## Learning Resources

**Tutorials and guides**

- [Color Metrics 101 (this repository)](guide/color-metrics-101.md) - guide/color-metrics-101.md. ΔE and its decomposition, aligned vs misaligned measurement, average-then-compare, the cast-vs-shift sanity check and what to report.
- [CIEDE2000 implementation notes and test data](https://hajim.rochester.edu/ece/sites/gsharma/ciede2000/) - Gaurav Sharma (University of Rochester). MATLAB and Excel code with the test pairs that catch common implementation mistakes.
- [ColorVideoVDP project page](https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/research/rainbow/projects/colorvideovdp/) - Rafał Mantiuk's group (Cambridge). Explains display models, JOD units and distortion maps for visible-difference prediction.
- [Using Colorcheck](https://docs.imatest.com/docs/colorcheck) - Imatest documentation. Practical chart-based color accuracy, ΔE vs ΔC, exposure and saturation pitfalls.
- [Understanding the In-Camera Rendering Pipeline and the Role of AI/Deep Learning](http://www.eecs.yorku.ca/~mbrown/ICCV2023_Brown.html) - Michael S. Brown (ICCV 2023 tutorial). Color science of the camera pipeline, the background for what ISP color metrics measure.

**Books**

- [Color Appearance Models, 3rd ed.](https://doi.org/10.1002/9781118653128) - Mark D. Fairchild (Wiley, 2013). Color appearance phenomena, CIECAM02 and the models behind modern uniform spaces.
- [Measuring Colour, 4th ed.](https://doi.org/10.1002/9781119975595) - R. W. G. Hunt and M. R. Pointer (Wiley, 2011). Colorimetry, color-difference formulas and their practical use.
- [Digital Color Imaging Handbook](https://doi.org/10.1201/9781420041484) - Gaurav Sharma (ed.), CRC Press. Color science for imaging systems, including color difference and device characterization.
- [Handbook of Image Quality](https://doi.org/10.1201/9780203910825) - Brian W. Keelan (CRC Press, 2002). Quality rulers, JND scales and the perceptual calibration behind CPIQ-style metrics.
- [Modern Image Quality Assessment](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-02238-8) - Zhou Wang and Alan C. Bovik (2006). Short monograph on full-reference IQA, from error visibility to structural similarity.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome: a missing metric, a new implementation, a correction to an alignment or color label, or a dead link. All content lives in the YAML files under [`data/`](data/); README.md, CODE.md and the interactive page are generated from them. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the entry format and the inclusion rules.

## About This List

**Why it exists.** A GitHub survey on 2026-10-11 found no curated list dedicated to color metrics. The closest are [Awesome-Image-Quality-Assessment](https://github.com/chaofengc/Awesome-Image-Quality-Assessment), whose "Color IQA" subsection has two entries, and [awesome-colour](https://github.com/colour-science/awesome-colour), which collects general color science resources without a metrics section. Neither says which metrics survive misaligned references.

**How entries were collected.** Starting points were the reference lists and citing papers of SPCD, CD-Flow, CD-iNet, MS-SWD, CD-Reasoning, ColorVideoVDP, HyAB, iCID and DeepSSIM (Semantic Scholar / OpenCitations), Crossref keyword searches, the evaluation sections of learned-ISP, burst and real-world super-resolution papers, ISO / IEEE camera standards, and the toolboxes listed above.

**How links and labels were checked.** Paper links were resolved through Crossref, arXiv or the publisher on 2026-10-11; repository READMEs were read to confirm official code and package names. Alignment labels follow what each paper claims or what its mechanism implies; *Tolerates small shifts* means sub-pixel to a few pixels, not arbitrary viewpoints. Color labels marked *partial* mean the paper does not test color. Please open an issue when a label is wrong or a link breaks.

**Known gaps.** Not a systematic review: IEEE Xplore and ACM DL were not searched exhaustively, and preprints that neither appear on arXiv nor cite the papers above may be missing. Out of scope: no-reference quality models without a color component, color constancy algorithms themselves (see Related Lists), colorization and color-transfer methods, and video-only temporal metrics.
